newsitem.title: USA: UPS returning to full operations Wednesday-CEO.
newsitem.headline: UPS returning to full operations Wednesday-CEO.

text.p: United Parcel Service will begin returning to full operations Wednesday, but the fate of thousands of striking Teamster members could remain in doubt for weeks, company Chairman James Kelly said Tuesday.

In a news conference at UPS headquarters, executives said the world's largest parcel delivery company would contact 1.6 million U.S. customers and make personal visits to hundreds of thousands in hopes of winning back business lost to the 15-day-old strike.

"The strike tomorrow will be ancient history," Kelly said of the walkout by 185,000 Teamster employees that has cost UPS $650 million since Aug. 4. "We have some limited operations today, and we expect to have a full total operation tomorrow."

A day after initialing a tentative agreement with the Teamsters union providing higher pay, more full-time jobs and heftier pension benefits, UPS defended the deal as being within acceptable financial "parameters" and said it would guarantee five years of labor stability.
Kelly acknowledged the company had compromised on a series of issues, however, particularly its demand that UPS leave a Teamster-run pension fund and set up an individual plan for UPS employees.

"Negotiation is a series of compromises, and there were dozens and dozens of issues that were compromised on. Unfortunately, the pension issue got the most press and that was the one where we compromised the most," he said.
